title: Time-Series Carry, 19 futures, monthly rebalance
hypothesis: time-series carry: long a market when its front contract trades above the second (backwardation, positive roll yield), short in contango. Annualized from the front and second contract (5-day mean), risk-scaled to equal volatility, rebalanced monthly. Carry is the compensation for holding the risky side of a futures curve and is a documented return source separate from price trend; low turnover means the cost model should matter little.

rules.signal: score = ln(front close / second close) * 365 / contract spacing (days between the previous two rolls), mean of the last 5 days; second contract = Databento .c.1 calendar-roll continuous series
rules.sizing: weight per market = sign(score) (tsmom) or +1/-1 by within-class rank (xsmom), times 10% target vol / 60-day realized vol, leverage capped at 3 per market, divided by number of active markets
rules.rebalance: last trading day of each month; weights decided at the close earn returns from the NEXT day
rules.implementation: src/research/dlt_engine.py + src/carry.py (committed, canonical, no tunable values)

author: claude-proposer
disclosure: Menu candidate chosen on economic grounds before any carry data was looked at. Spacing between contracts is proxied from the previous two rolls, so the first ~6 months per market have no carry. Ags have irregular cycles, so their annualization is rough. RTY history starts 2017-07. Roll-day returns are set to 0.

pass_criteria.conditions: net Sharpe >= 0.3 in discovery AND net Sharpe >= 0.3 in validation AND validation cumulative net return > 0
pass_criteria.supported: conditions met AND validation Deflated Sharpe Ratio >= 0.95
pass_criteria.inconclusive: conditions met but the Deflated Sharpe Ratio is below 0.95
